prompt.context_jp: その名前が出た途端、相馬の表情___みるみる曇った。
prompt.prompt_jp: その名前が出た途端、相馬の表情___みるみる曇った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits best.

feedback.correct_en: This describes a new, observed change — Souma's expression suddenly darkening. が marks this fresh, event-level observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 相馬の表情 as an already-established topic being commented on, which clashes with the sudden, perceived change happening in the moment.

prompt.context_jp: 振り返った舞の目に、戸口に立つ細身の男の姿___映った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 振り返った舞の目に、戸口に立つ細身の男の姿___映った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Himuro is being introduced here — a new figure appearing in Mai's sight. New-information が is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the man was already a topic in the discussion, but he is just now entering the scene.

prompt.context_jp: 私___今回の与信検査の指揮を執る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___今回の与信検査の指揮を執る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Himuro uses.

feedback.correct_en: Himuro is asserting exhaustively that HE — and no one else — is in charge. This is exhaustive-listing が, matching his authoritative self-introduction.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would merely topicalize himself; it loses the 'I'm the one in charge here' emphasis Himuro is projecting.

contrast_examples.en: I am the one in charge.
I'm the person in charge. (as for me)

prompt.context_jp: 氷室の視線___舞の欄の上でぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 氷室の視線___舞の欄の上でぴたりと止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A specific, observable event — Himuro's gaze stopping. が marks the subject of this new, moment-of-action observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 氷室の視線 into a general topic, which doesn't fit this punctual single event.

prompt.context_jp: 下町の風情が残るこの界隈___、舞にとって子どもの頃から慣れ親しんだ庭のような場所だ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 下町の風情が残るこの界隈___、舞にとって…庭のような場所だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence takes 'this neighborhood' as the topic and comments on what it is to Mai. は fits a defining/characterizing statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as new information in an event, but this is a general, categorical description of the area for Mai.

prompt.context_jp: どうせ それぐらいしか できないだろう
prompt.prompt_jp: どうせ それぐらい___できないだろう
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures Himuro's dismissive meaning?

feedback.correct_en: しか + negative means 'only that much' — expressing that Mai is capable of nothing more. This matches Himuro's belittling tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: は or が would lose the 'only this and nothing else' nuance. しか…ない is the fixed pattern for limiting negatives.

prompt.context_jp: どの会社のファイルに氷室の目___留まるのか、誰にも予想はつかなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: どの会社のファイルに氷室の目___留まるのか…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the embedded question.

feedback.correct_en: Inside an embedded wh-question clause ('which file his eye would stop on'), が marks the subject naturally. は would conflict with the question focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to topicalize 氷室の目, but the clause itself is asking which file catches the eye — a focus-identification context that requires が.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が来るか分からない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't know who will come.

prompt.context_jp: 化粧室で整えた笑顔___、今のところまだ崩れていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 化粧室で整えた笑顔___、今のところまだ崩れていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The smile was already a known/established thing (fixed in the restroom). は takes it as the topic and comments 'as for it, hasn't broken yet.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame the smile as new information being introduced, but it has already been mentioned/implied in the previous scene.

contrast_examples.jp: その笑顔はまだ消えない。

prompt.context_jp: 舞には知らされていないこと___、実はひとつあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞には知らされていないこと___、実はひとつあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces something new — 'there was one thing Mai wasn't told.' Existential 'ある' with new info takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require that 'the thing' already be an established topic, but the narrator is introducing it for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: そうだね 彼女 すぐ顔___出るから
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女、すぐ顔___出るから
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'face' here.

feedback.correct_en: 顔に出る is a set collocation — 'it shows on her face.' The emotion appears on the face (location/direction), so に is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the face as the location of an action; を would make it an object. Neither fits this idiomatic 'show on' phrase.

prompt.context_jp: 与信検査の結果___人事査定にも大きく影響するからね
prompt.prompt_jp: 与信検査の結果___人事査定にも大きく影響するからね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a general, categorical statement: 'credit inspection results (as a rule) affect HR evaluations.' Generic/characterizing claims take は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as a specific event-subject, but Karashima is stating a general truth about how the system works.

prompt.context_jp: その横顔には、…揺るぎない自信___にじんでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: …揺るぎない自信___にじんでいる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The confidence is being newly described/observed oozing from his profile. This introductory observation needs が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose 自信 as an already-topicalized thing, which doesn't fit descriptive narration bringing it up for the first time.

prompt.context_jp: 深川支店___たるんでんじゃないんですか
prompt.prompt_jp: 深川支店___たるんでんじゃないんですか
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Himuro's accusatory contrast?

feedback.correct_en: Himuro singles out Fukagawa Branch as the topic of criticism, contrasting it (implicitly) with other, better branches. Contrastive/topical は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a neutral subject-marking, losing the pointed 'as for this branch — you people are slacking' accusation.

contrast_examples.jp: この支店はたるんでいる。

prompt.context_jp: 私が聞いてるの___ここに書いてない情報だ！
prompt.prompt_jp: 私が聞いてるの___ここに書いてない情報だ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 'What I'm asking about は X' — the nominalized clause is the topic/frame, and the predicate specifies what it IS. Standard A は B identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the whole structure ungrammatical here; the identificational copular sentence requires は for the topic nominal.

contrast_examples.jp: 私が欲しいのは時間だ。

prompt.context_jp: 深川プリントの担当___君なんだよな？
prompt.prompt_jp: 深川プリントの担当___君なんだよな？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for who's in charge of Fukagawa Print, it's you' — the topic is 担当 and 君 identifies it. A は B identification pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reverse the information flow; the known/presupposed thing (担当) is the topic, and 君 is the new answer.

contrast_examples.en: The person in charge is him.
HE is the one in charge.

prompt.context_jp: 窓口に立っていた頃なら、お客さまの前___こんな顔をすることなど絶対になかったはずだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: お客さまの前___こんな顔をすることなど絶対になかったはずだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place — 'in front of customers' is where she'd be making the face.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static location or destination, not the setting of an activity like 'making a face.' を doesn't fit at all.

prompt.context_jp: 氷室主任を紹介する場面
prompt.prompt_jp: 人___“支店荒らし”
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank in '人___"支店荒らし"' meaning 'they call him the branch destroyer.'

feedback.correct_en: 「人呼んで〜」is a set phrase meaning 'known as / they call him —.' It introduces a nickname or epithet.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言って or 叫んで don't form the fixed epithet-introducing idiom. 人呼んで is the frozen expression.

contrast_examples.jp: みんなが鬼と呼んでいる。

prompt.context_jp: 氷室が舞に言う言葉
prompt.prompt_jp: 我々の足を___ないでくれ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: 'don't ___ our feet' (= don't hold us back).

feedback.correct_en: 足を引っ張る is the fixed idiom for 'to hold someone back / be a drag on them.' Himuro is telling Mai not to be a hindrance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 押さえる or 止める don't form this idiom. The verb paired with 足 in this metaphor is specifically 引っ張る.

contrast_examples.jp: チームの足を引っ張る。

prompt.context_jp: 児玉が田山支店長に厳しく念押しする場面
prompt.prompt_jp: …ということを ___に銘じておいていただきたい！
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank in the idiom meaning 'keep firmly in mind.'

feedback.correct_en: 肝に銘じる is the set phrase for 'engrave in one's liver = take deeply to heart.' Kodama is making a stern warning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心に銘じる or 頭に銘じる are not idiomatic. The fixed collocation uses 肝 specifically.

contrast_examples.en: Take the failure deeply to heart.

prompt.context_jp: 地位と権力を___に着ちゃってるんだ
prompt.prompt_jp: 地位と権力を___に着ちゃってるんだ
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank in the idiom meaning 'wearing authority like a shield.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜を笠に着る is the fixed idiom for 'exploit/hide behind one's authority.' The 笠 is a traditional sedge hat used as a metaphorical shield.
feedback.incorrect_en: 傘 (umbrella) sounds the same but is wrong; 背に着る is not an idiom. Only 笠 fits this set phrase.

prompt.context_jp: 舞が氷室について不満をぶつける場面
prompt.prompt_jp: ちょっとのミスを___取ってネチネチ…
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the blank: ___を取る meaning 'nitpick, catch on a slip.'

feedback.correct_en: 揚げ足を取る is the idiom for 'catch someone's slip / nitpick' — originally from sumo/judo, grabbing a lifted leg.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下足 means footwear check; 片足 just means 'one leg.' Neither forms the nitpicking idiom.

prompt.context_jp: それって ___融資じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_jp: それって ___融資じゃないですか
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: the term for lending that is routed through a third party.

feedback.correct_en: 迂回融資 means 'circumvented/indirect lending' — using a third company to route money that can't be lent directly. That's exactly what's suspected here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 直接融資 means 'direct lending' (the opposite); 短期融資 means 'short-term loan.' Neither matches the illegal scheme described.

prompt.context_jp: 最近 臨店がないから もう 体が___ちゃって…
prompt.prompt_jp: 体が___ちゃって…
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: Mai says she's getting out of shape.

feedback.correct_en: 体が鈍る means 'to become out of shape / lose one's edge from inactivity.' Perfect for Mai complaining about lack of fieldwork.
feedback.incorrect_en: 疲れる means 'get tired' (opposite — needs activity); 痩せる is just 'lose weight.' Neither captures 'getting rusty.'

prompt.context_jp: 深川支店長が検査部一行を出迎える場面
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらの支店長の挨拶が最も自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds most natural from a branch manager welcoming inspectors?

choices.text: どうも ご足労おかけいたしまして 支店長の田山でございます
わざわざ来てくれて ありがとう 支店長の田山だよ

feedback.correct_en: ご足労おかけいたしまして + でございます is the appropriate humble/formal register for a branch manager greeting superiors from HQ.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual for a workplace greeting to visiting inspectors; C is blunt and inappropriately curt for the hierarchy.

contrast_examples.jp: ご足労いただきありがとうございます。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for making the trip. (formal)

contrast_examples.jp: 来てくれてありがとう。

prompt.context_jp: 氷室が江藤を厳しく叱責する場面
prompt.prompt_jp: 氷室の叱責として最も自然な表現は？
prompt.prompt_en: Which best fits Himuro's harsh dressing-down tone?

choices.text: そのぐらい見抜けないようじゃ 融資マン失格！
そのぐらい見抜けないと ちょっと困りますね
見抜けなくても 大丈夫ですよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜ようじゃ…失格 is a blunt condemnatory pattern fitting Himuro's harsh, superior tone that the chapter emphasizes.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is a soft complaint, not consistent with the 'branch destroyer' persona. C is reassurance — the opposite of Himuro's attitude.

contrast_examples.jp: これができないようじゃ失格だ。
contrast_examples.en: If you can't do this, you're unfit.

prompt.context_jp: 小料理屋で舞が氷室について愚痴る場面
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞のくだけた言い方として自然なのはどれですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits Mai's casual, frustrated outburst most naturally?

choices.text: 何なんですか あのクソ主任！
あの主任は少し問題があると思います
氷室様におかれましては ご立派で…

feedback.correct_en: 何なんですか + 'クソ主任' captures Mai's frustrated outburst — informal, emotional, with mild vulgarity Souma immediately scolds.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is politely restrained — doesn't match her exploding anger. C is honorific/ironic praise — totally wrong register for a venting rant.

contrast_examples.jp: あの方は少々難しい方です。
contrast_examples.en: That person is a bit difficult. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 田山支店長が氷室の要求に応じる場面
prompt.prompt_jp: 支店長の答えとして最も自然なのはどれ？
prompt.prompt_en: Which response fits the branch manager's deferential, cornered position?

choices.text: 分かりました 明日の朝 必ずお渡ししますので
了解 あした渡すね
それはちょっと考えておきます

feedback.correct_en: 分かりました + 必ずお渡しします is firm, polite, and shows submissive compliance — fitting a branch manager cornered into bribery.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is far too casual for addressing a superior inspector; C is an evasive 'I'll think about it' which doesn't match the desperate agreement scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 必ずお渡しいたします。

prompt.context_jp: 舞が北村課長を安心させようとする場面
prompt.prompt_jp: どちらの表現がこの場面で最も自然ですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing captures Mai's reassurance most naturally?

choices.text: 私たち臨店班は 支店の皆さまの味方ですから
私たち臨店班は 支店の皆さまのお友達ですから
私たち臨店班は 支店の皆さまの応援ですから

feedback.correct_en: 味方 ('ally/on your side') is the natural idiom when reassuring colleagues under pressure. It evokes solidarity.
feedback.incorrect_en: お友達 is far too childish for a workplace setting; 応援 ('cheer/support') is not used as a predicate noun for 'we are your —' this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はあなたの味方です。
